title: ASSIGNING A STREAM TO A MEMBER HAS NEVER WORKED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE - membership.member_streams.StreamId IS AN IDENTITY COLUMN, so every assignment throws 'Cannot insert explicit value for identity column'. ADR-0043 steps 3 and 4 both shipped on top of it. Found 2026-08-14 by the step-5 backfill's own integration test, which failed in SETUP rather than in its assertion - the setup was the first code in this repository ever to assign a stream against SQL Server. THE MEASUREMENT, and the second half is the production path rather than a test artefact: (1) 20260625045056_Membership_P4_Identity.cs:80-82 creates member_streams with `StreamId = table.Column<long>(...).Annotation('SqlServer:Identity', '1, 1')`, and MembershipDbContextModelSnapshot:264-268 agreed - ValueGeneratedOnAdd + UseIdentityColumn. The cause is an EF convention rather than an author's choice: for an OwnsMany with a composite key, the non-foreign-key half is treated as store-generated, and CommitteeMemberConfiguration:39 declared `sa.Property(s => s.StreamId)` without overriding it. (2) A test mirroring AssignStreamsHandler EXACTLY - load an existing member, call member.AssignStreams(new[]{ coreStreamId }) with an id read from the streams table, SaveChangesAsync - threw DbUpdateException wrapping SqlException 'Cannot insert explicit value for identity column in table member_streams when IDENTITY_INSERT is set to OFF'. That is a measurement of the shipped path, not an inference from the DDL. WHAT WAS BROKEN, and it was two of this slice's own steps: PUT /api/members/{publicId}/streams (AssignStreamsHandler, step 3, 71283ad) failed for any non-empty selection, and the FR-156 invite (InviteUserHandler, step 4, af98621) failed at its SECOND SaveChanges - after the Keycloak account and the member row already existed, so the caller saw an error while a real account was left behind with no streams. Clearing a member's streams to EMPTY still worked, because that writes only deletes. ⚠ WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, which is the generalisable half: Acmp.Api.Tests runs on the EF InMemory provider, which has no identity columns and accepts an explicitly-set key that SQL Server refuses - the precise contrast Acmp.Integration.Tests exists to draw, and no integration test had ever written a member_streams row. The e2e stack does use SQL Server, but it runs with KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED=false so the invite path never executes, and there is no e2e that assigns streams. Domain tests exercise the aggregate with no database at all. So four suites all passed while the feature could not work once. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #266 (squash 0464979), landing with ADR-0043 step 5 because the backfill's explicit INSERT hits the same rule. The override went in the SHARED configuration - `sa.Property(s => s.StreamId).ValueGeneratedNever()` in CommitteeMemberConfiguration - rather than at either call site. ⚠ EF CANNOT SCAFFOLD THE SCHEMA HALF: its generated AlterColumn dropping the annotation throws 'To change the IDENTITY property of a column, the column needs to be dropped and recreated', because SQL Server has no ALTER for it. Migration Membership_MemberStreamsNoIdentity_DEF066 therefore rebuilds the table by hand (create -> copy -> drop -> sp_rename), ordered immediately BEFORE the backfill, and COPIES rows rather than dropping the column. ⚠ IT ALSO REFUSES TO CARRY AN ORPHAN: member_streams has no FK to streams and the identity generated 1, 2, 3..., so a row naming an Id no stream holds is possible; UserStreamProvider inner-joins, so such a row is merely invisible today but would silently scope that member to whatever stream holds that number once step 7 wires StreamScopeRequirement. A wrong scope is worse than an absent one, so the migration stops the deployment and names what it found rather than copying it or deleting it silently. All ten PR checks green including e2e.

title: A FRONTEND TEST FAILS INTERMITTENTLY UNDER COVERAGE AND IT IS PRE-EXISTING - DecisionPage.test.tsx 'requires a condition when the successor is Conditionally Approved, then submits it'. Found 2026-08-14 while gating the AC-034 edit flow: `npm run test:cov` reported a failure that `vitest run` did not. ⚠ THE FIRST INSTINCT WAS WRONG AND WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Because the failure appeared in the same run as newly-added tests, the obvious reading was that the new work caused it. IT DID NOT: the run was repeated with every source change STASHED, and DecisionPage.test.tsx failed on the bare baseline too. Authorship was measured, not argued from plausibility. THE OBSERVATIONS: the file passes 15/15 when run ALONE, passes in a plain full `vitest run` (1206/1206, twice), and fails only under `test:cov` - and not on every coverage run, which is what makes it flaky rather than broken. Coverage instrumentation slows every test in the process, so this is the classic load-sensitive async assertion: the same shape as DEF-061 on the e2e side and the same class as the recorded 'localhost CI hides load races' finding. A developer machine settles the interaction before the assertion and never sees it; a loaded runner does not. WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING LOW: `test:cov` is what CI's frontend job runs, so this can turn an unrelated PR red, and an intermittently red gate is how a blocking check becomes something people re-run without reading - the exact failure mode this project has already recorded for advisories. title: STEP 7's BLAST RADIUS WAS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT DEF-062 PREDICTED, AND THE REAL LANDMINE WAS A TEST STUB, NOT THE E2E SUITE. THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong because it reasoned from ROLES rather than from CALL SITES. THE MEASUREMENT, four facts: (1) Policies.TopicEdit is the ONLY stream-bounded policy evaluated WITH a resource - TopicTriage and BacklogPrioritize allow Chairman/Secretary only (who bypass), TopicSubmit is endpoint-level with no resource at all, and DiagramAttach has no EnsureAsync call site anywhere. (2) Every e2e caller of a TopicEdit-gated route is a SECRETARY: apiHelpers.prepareTopic passes the secretary bearer (its own comment says so), scenario.ts prepares with the secretary, core-loop.spec.ts marks Prepared through the Secretary's UI session, and ac049-upload-l10n.spec.ts uploads attachments as loginAs(page,'secretary'). (3) topic-scope.spec.ts's Member assertions ALREADY EXPECT 403 - so they stayed green, though for a second reason. (4) Acmp.Api.Tests' TopicEdit paths are the submitter editing pre-Accept (no authorization at all) or a Secretary. ✅ CI SETTLED IT EMPIRICALLY: PR #269 wired the requirement and the e2e job PASSED. ⚠ THE ACTUAL LANDMINE, and it failed CLOSED and LOUDLY rather than open: PermissionMatrixTests evaluates every registered policy against `StubTopic : ITopicScopedResource`, which does NOT implement IStreamScopedResource, AND it evaluates the 'A' cells with NO RESOURCE AT ALL. The stub was only the messenger: the same shape refuses ANY call site passing a non-stream-scoped resource. So the test now ASSERTS THE REAL PROPERTY - a stream-scoped policy is RESOURCE-ONLY and cannot be decided without a resource - and AuthorizationRegistration.StreamScoped carries the rule for adding a policy to that set: only where every call site passes a stream-scoped aggregate. The stub implements IStreamScopedResource with a stream the principal holds, so the matrix test stays about the CAPABILITY matrix (§C) instead of silently becoming a stream-scope test (§E.1). title: RUNNING THE COVERAGE GATE LOCALLY MORE THAN ONCE MADE IT REPORT ON CODE THAT NO LONGER EXISTED - check-coverage.mjs merged EVERY cobertura report under tests/*/TestResults, and `dotnet test --collect` writes a NEW timestamped directory on every run instead of replacing the last one. Found 2026-08-14 during ADR-0043 step 7, and it cost two speculative changes before it was caught. THE SYMPTOM: the gate failed with `50.00% (1/2) AbacProviders.cs` and kept failing with the identical figure after the only coverable code in that file had been MOVED OUT of it. A file with no code cannot be 50% covered, which is what made the measurement suspect rather than the code. THE MEASUREMENT: 30 TestResults directories had accumulated across one session's repeated runs; the script walked the tree from the repo root and summed every coverage.cobertura.xml it found, so a file edited between runs was scored against its OLD self as well as its new one and the worst historical reading won. Deleting tests/*/TestResults and re-running turned the same commit from FAIL to PASS. ⚠ CI WAS UNAFFECTED, which is exactly why it survived: every CI run starts from a fresh checkout with no TestResults at all, so the gate was correct there and wrong only on the machine of anyone following the project's own standing advice to run the gates locally before pushing. ⚠ A STALE GATE DOES NOT MERELY WASTE TIME, IT DIRECTS WORK: two changes were made to satisfy the false reading before the reading itself was doubted. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 in PR #273 (squash d42ae7c) per DEC-047: the script now takes only the NEWEST report per test project and logs how many it ignored. Keyed on the TestResults parent, so a solution-wide run still measures every project - just once each, at its latest run. ⚠ THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN LOG LINE CAUGHT IT, which is worth recording because the failure mode is the same class as the defect: the grouping key split the path on a hand-written /[\/]/ character class, which matches FORWARD SLASHES ONLY, while node's join() produces BACKSLASHES on Windows. Every key collapsed to the empty string, all five reports landed in one bucket, four legitimate per-project reports were discarded, and the gate reported 84.70% - a FALSE FAILURE, which is worse than the stale reading it replaced. It announced 'ignoring 4 superseded report(s)', and that line - added on instinct so the reader would be told rather than silently given a merge - is the only reason the failure was diagnosable rather than mysterious. Replaced with dirname twice, which has no separator to hand-write. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a clean full run reports 99.61% and ignores nothing; a planted stale duplicate with an older mtime is ignored rather than merged.

title: ANY BRANCH CUT BEFORE 4c1b356 SILENTLY RE-INTRODUCED DEF-064's MOJIBAKE WHEN MERGED, AND NOTHING IN THE BUILD COULD SEE IT. Caught 2026-08-14 in the act, while rebasing fix/admin-streams-tab-live onto main under DEC-046. THE MEASUREMENT: the ar.json rebase conflict's BRANCH side carried mojibake where main carries correct Arabic - five pre-existing keys (admin.streams.title/help/noneWarning/save/saved) still holding the exact UTF-8-read-as-Latin-1 corruption that 4c1b356 repaired. The branch predates that repair, so its file is simply the old broken one plus its own additions. Taking the branch side of that hunk - the ordinary thing to do when a branch is 'the one changing this section' - would have re-shipped the defect. ⚠ WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, and this is the part that generalises: check-i18n.mjs compared KEY SETS, not values, so parity was 'OK' over mojibake and said so cheerfully; the ENGLISH half of every affected string is untouched, so no screen looks wrong to a reviewer who does not read Arabic; and the corruption is valid UTF-8 text, so no encoding check, linter or type-checker had anything to object to. DEF-064 records the same blindness from the WRITING side; this row records it from the MERGING side, which is worse because the person merging did not write the string and has no reason to look at it. RESOLVED IN THE MERGE by keeping MAIN's correct Arabic for the five pre-existing keys and taking only the branch's genuinely new ones (col.stream, col.code, and the reworded empty state), RETYPED as literal UTF-8 rather than copied from the mojibake side - copying from the conflict's branch half is how the corruption would propagate even in a 'careful' resolution. ✅ THE CLASS IS NOW CLOSED, not just this instance: PR #273 (squash d42ae7c) adds a VALUE-LEVEL guard to check-i18n.mjs. Arabic encoded UTF-8 then decoded as Latin-1 always lands in the Ø/Ù/Ã block, and correct Arabic never contains those characters at all - so ONE is enough, with no threshold to tune and no way for a partially corrupted string to slip under it. Proven by injecting REAL DEF-064 corruption (.encode('utf-8').decode('latin-1')) into a value and confirming the guard names the key and EXITS 1, and that a clean file exits 0 - a gate that prints without failing is the shape this project has been burned by before. It now catches the writing side, the merging side, and every future branch at once, which is why it was chosen over rebasing the stale branches or documenting 'inspect ar.json conflicts by eye' - the latter relies on exactly the attention that fails here.

title: DEC-046's RECONCILIATION IS INERT FOR DEF-065 UNLESS IT ASSIGNS THE WILDCARD ITSELF - creating the member rows is necessary and NOT sufficient, because the backfill that would have covered them has already run by then. Found 2026-08-14 while scoping the reconciliation, by asking WHEN the migration runs relative to WHEN reconciliation would create rows. ⚠ THE DECISION IS NOT WRONG - ITS MECHANISM IS ONE CLAUSE SHORT. DEC-046 chose to 'reconcile Keycloak accounts into committee_members BEFORE the step-7 deploy, so the rows exist for the backfill to reach', and that is the right shape. The gap is in the word BEFORE: reconciliation is an APPLICATION FEATURE, so it can only run on a host that is already up - and Program.cs:133 applies migrations at BOOT, before the first HTTP request is served. The deploy that carries the reconciliation feature therefore also carries and RUNS the step-5 backfill first, against whatever rows exist at that moment, which is the same ~1 row DEF-065 describes. An administrator then reconciles, creating ~25 rows with ZERO streams - each of which is stream-bounded, and every one of them is refused every guarded write from their first login. That is exactly the outcome DEF-065 exists to prevent, reached by a different route. THE MEASUREMENT: Program.cs:133 runs MigrationRunner.MigrateAsync(app) during startup; the only two paths that write member_streams are AssignStreamsHandler (the Administrator-only PUT) and InviteUserHandler, and neither is part of any reconciliation. So nothing between 'row created by reconciliation' and 'member signs in' assigns a stream. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: the reconciliation command must assign the WILDCARD to every row IT CREATES - doing precisely what the backfill would have done had the row existed - rather than leaving assignment to a separate administrative step. ⚠ IT MUST APPLY ONLY TO ROWS IT CREATES, never to rows that already exist: an administrator may have deliberately narrowed someone to one stream, and widening that to the wildcard on a reconciliation run would silently hand them universal write access. This is the same asymmetry the step-5 backfill already encodes with its NOT EXISTS clause, and the reconciliation should encode it the same way. ⚠ A SECOND, SEPARATE OBSTACLE, recorded here so it is not discovered halfway: IIdentityProvider HAS NO READ OPERATION. Its four methods are CreateUser, SetRealmRoles, SignOutEverywhere and DisableUser, and its own comment states the narrowness is deliberate - 'no general-purpose call-Keycloak escape hatch, so the blast radius of the service-account credential is bounded by this interface'. Reconciliation needs to LIST realm users with their roles, which is a fifth operation on an ADR-0038-governed port. A bounded READ is consistent with that rationale (a read cannot mutate the identity provider) but it is a real widening of a surface that was narrowed on purpose, and it should be recorded as such rather than slipped in. ✅ FIXED 2026-08-14 by PR #275 (9508eef), built from the corrected mechanism rather than discovering the gap afterwards. BOTH clauses are implemented and BOTH are mutation-proven: creating the row and granting the wildcard are ONE operation in ReconcileIdentityAccountsHandler, and the grant applies only to rows that run creates. The port widening was recorded as SC-011 BEFORE the interface change existed in code. ⚠ THE ASYMMETRY NEEDED A TEST THAT DID NOT EXIST AT FIRST REVIEW: 'wildcard everyone' is caught by a member narrowed to one stream, but the subtler wrong implementation - 'wildcard any member holding ZERO streams' - was caught by NOTHING, because no test carried a pre-existing zero-stream member. That is the plausible later 'fix', and it is wrong for a reason invisible from the data: an administrator can clear a member's streams deliberately and member_streams has no provenance column to tell the two apart. It is now pinned by Reconcile_leaves_a_pre_existing_member_holding_NO_streams_alone, which is the sole test that mutant fails.

title: I TURNED G-COMPLETE RED BY QUOTING A DESIGN FILE'S TEMPLATE SYNTAX INTO THE APPEND-ONLY PROGRESS JOURNAL, AND THE JOURNAL CANNOT BE EDITED TO TAKE IT BACK. Found 2026-08-14 by running gate_run() after recording DEF-041's fix - the gate went from 7/7 to fail with three findings, all of them rows I had just written. WHAT HAPPENED: ACMP Administration.dc.html is a template, so the control it draws appears in the file as an element whose click handler is a mustache expression. Quoting that verbatim into two progress entries and a defect title was the natural way to evidence the INV-014 finding about where the voting toggle belongs. G-COMPLETE screens content for unfinished-work markers, and its pattern list ends with an empty mustache expression - the very token an unfinished template leaves behind - so faithfully quoted evidence and an unfinished document are indistinguishable to it. THE MEASUREMENT, not a guess: tamheed_server.py defines the screen as the usual unfinished-work words plus an angle-bracket filler token, a mustache expression and a filler-text phrase; the call site strips code spans FIRST, with a comment saying such markers inside code spans are example text rather than unfinished markers. So the escape is designed and documented in the source: BACKTICK ANY QUOTED TEMPLATE SYNTAX. WHY IT WAS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: progress_entries is an APPEND-ONLY JOURNAL. entity_upsert on an existing PE- id is refused by a UNIQUE constraint whose error message says corrections are recorded as new entries, not edits - correct design, and exactly why the mistake was expensive. A defect TITLE is mutable and was simply rewritten; two progress entries were not. HOW IT WAS REPAIRED, through the sanctioned path rather than by hand: the runtime store is an always-fresh in-memory SQLite rebuilt from the canonical JSONL on every open (store.py), and the recorded procedure for a bad write is 'rollback is git only'. So: package_close to release and flush, a WHOLE-FILE git checkout of progress_entries.jsonl at the last commit before the bad entries, package_open to rebuild the store from the restored file, then re-append the entries with the template token in backticks. That is a whole-file git rollback, not a hand-edit of package data; it left PE-325..PE-327 untouched and reallocated the same ids to the corrected entries, so no gap appears. ⚠ AND THE FIX ITSELF TRIPPED THE GATE ONCE MORE, which is the funniest and most useful part of this row: the FIRST version of this very title spelled out the marker words it was describing, so a defect ABOUT the placeholder screen was caught BY the placeholder screen. Describing a pattern counts as writing it. ⚠ THE GENERAL LESSON IS NOT ABOUT MUSTACHES: the package is PROSE ABOUT CODE, so any syntax quoted into it is read by the gates as if it were the package's own text. Code-span every quoted fragment. ⚠ AND THE SHARPER ONE: run gate_run() AFTER writing, not only before. Had I closed the session on the merge, main would have carried a red critical gate with the failing rows immutable, and the next session would have inherited both.
